scenario: A mountain-tourism researcher analyses alpine huts featured in quality-review guides, all of which survived multiple avalanche seasons. Mean visitor-satisfaction score among reviewed huts is 7.2 (σ=1.4) on a 10-point scale; the review-inclusion threshold is 5.0. The true mean satisfaction across all huts built in a given decade is sought.

data.description: Observed statistics among units that cleared the survival/publication filter

values.note: Only units above the survival threshold appear in the observed sample

question: (a) Assuming visitor satisfaction score is normally distributed with σ=1.4 score points in the full pre-filter cohort, solve numerically for the true pre-filter population mean μ such that E[X | X > 5.0] = 7.2. (b) What fraction of all original units cleared the survival filter? (c) By how much (in score points) does the survivor mean overstate μ? (d) What policy or scientific conclusion error arises from ignoring the survival filter?

ground_truth.explanation: The alpine mountain huts in tourism-quality reviews dataset is a truncated-normal sample above the survival threshold t=5.0 score points. Solving E[X|X>t]=μ+σφ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=7.2 numerically gives μ=6.97602 score points. Only 92.09% of the original cohort survived; the observed mean overstates the true mean by 0.22398 score points. Ignoring the filter leads to over-estimating the baseline quality/capacity of the full cohort, producing over-optimistic policy conclusions.

naive_answer: The true mean visitor satisfaction score is 7.2 score points because that is the average observed among the surviving/studied units.
naive_trap: The observed sample consists only of units above the survival threshold. The observed mean is E[X|X>5.0] — a truncated conditional expectation — not the population mean. It systematically overstates μ whenever the threshold is non-trivially binding.
reasoning_trace: (1) Survival filter ≡ truncated-normal sampling with lower truncation at t=5.0. (2) E[X|X>t] = μ + σ·φ((t−μ)/σ) / Φ̄((t−μ)/σ) = 7.2. (3) Solve numerically via brentq on [-30.0, 7.1999] → μ=6.97602. (4) Fraction above threshold: Φ̄((5.0−6.97602)/1.4) = 0.92094. (5) Overstatement: 7.2−6.97602 = 0.22398 score points.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 7.2,1.4,5.0
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-25*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=300)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-6.97602)<0.005, f'mu={mu_sol:.5f}'
assert abs(frac-0.92094)<0.005, f'frac={frac:.5f}'
assert mu_sol < obs
assert abs((obs-mu_sol)-0.22398)<0.01
